steps.tx: High-resolution manometry is the clinical gold standard for assessing motor dysfunction of the oesophagus. According to the **Chicago Classification** version **4.0**, primary achalasia requires an elevated median **integrated relaxation pressure** exceeding **15** mmHg with Sierra or Medtronic solid-state assemblies, or exceeding **28** mmHg with Diversatek systems. This elevated pressure must occur alongside **100%** failed peristalsis across all test swallows, establishing impaired relaxation of the lower oesophageal sphincter.

steps.tx: High-resolution manometry separates achalasia into three distinct operational subtypes based on pressurization patterns. **Type I achalasia** or classic achalasia demonstrates **100%** failed peristalsis without significant esophageal pressurization. In contrast, **Type II achalasia** exhibits panesophageal pressurization in at least **20%** of swallows, generating compression between the upper and lower sphincters. **Type III achalasia** or spastic achalasia shows premature spastic contractions with reduced distal latency in at least **20%** of swallows.

left.title: Type I and II Achalasia
points: Type I: 100% failed peristalsis with aperistalsis
Type II: Panesophageal pressurization in >= 20% swallows
Type II: Highest clinical response to balloon dilatation and myotomy

right.title: Type III Spastic Achalasia
points: Type III: Premature spastic contractions in >= 20% swallows
Poor response to standard balloon dilatation
Requires extended length peroral endoscopic myotomy

steps.tx: **Peroral endoscopic myotomy** has revolutionized definitive interventional management for all three **achalasia subtypes**. By creating a submucosal tunnel in the mid-oesophagus and dividing the inner circular muscle layer, POEM achieves high clinical success rates exceeding ninety percent. Crucially, POEM allows the operator to extend the myotomy proximally into the esophageal body. This tailored proximal extension is essential for managing **Type III achalasia**, where extensive spastic contractility fails to respond to standard distal disruption.

nodes.label: Clip closure of mucosal entry site

steps.tx: **Pneumatic balloon dilatation** remains an established first-line non-surgical treatment for achalasia, particularly in Type II disease. The technique utilizes graded low-compliance Rigiflex polyethylene balloons measuring **30** mm, **35** mm, and **40** mm in diameter to mechanically tear circular muscle fibres of the **lower esophageal sphincter**. Dilatations proceed sequentially under fluoroscopic guidance, starting with the 30 mm balloon. The procedure carries an inherent **2%** to **3%** risk of transmural oesophageal perforation.

steps.tx: **Distal esophageal spasm** represents a severe hypermotility disorder defined under high-resolution manometry criteria. Diagnostic confirmation requires a normal integrated relaxation pressure combined with premature contractions in at least **20%** of test swallows. The key physiological metric is a shortened **distal latency** of less than **4.5** seconds from upper sphincter relaxation to the contractile deceleration point. Patients typically present with episodic retrosternal chest pain and dysphagia that mimic acute coronary syndromes.

steps.tx: **Jackhammer esophagus** is a profound state of hypercontractility characterized by excessively vigorous smooth muscle peristalsis. The diagnosis is confirmed on high-resolution manometry when at least **20%** of test swallows exhibit a **distal contractile integral** exceeding **8000** mmHg-s-cm, in the presence of normal lower oesophageal sphincter relaxation. Repetitive prolonged multi-peaked contractions cause intermittent dysphagia and severe non-cardiac chest pain, reflecting extreme muscular hypertrophy of the tubular esophagus.

steps.tx: **Esophagogastric junction outflow obstruction** is identified when high-resolution manometry reveals an elevated median integrated relaxation pressure alongside **preserved peristalsis** that fails to meet full criteria for achalasia. Because elevated junctional pressure can arise from mechanical compression, strictures, hiatal hernia, or early occult achalasia, diagnostic evaluation mandates barium esophagography and endoscopic ultrasound. Timed barium swallow confirms true functional delay before considering invasive lower sphincter interventions.

nodes.label: Rule out malignancy, stricture, or pseudoachalasia

steps.tx: **Chagas disease** represents an endemic parasitic infection caused by Trypanosoma cruzi that serves as the classical infectious cause of secondary achalasia. Chronic infection leads to autoimmune, parasite-driven inflammatory destruction of postganglionic parasympathetic neurons in the intramural **Auerbach myenteric plexus**. Loss of inhibitory nitric oxide and VIP synthesis results in uninhibited basal sphincter tone, aperistalsis, severe megaesophagus, and concurrent megacolon, pathologically mimicking idiopathic achalasia.

left.title: Idiopathic Achalasia
points: Autoimmune destruction of myenteric inhibitory neurons
No concurrent colonic or cardiac dilatation
